99	def no_padding_2_padding(tensor: torch.Tensor, data: TensorDict) -> torch.Tensor:
100	    """Slice response from unpad model output.
101	
102	    Args:
103	        tensor: a nested tensor or a tensor of shape (total_nnz,*),
104	            total_nnz is the total number of tokens across all sequences in the batch
105	
106	        data: TensorDict with "prompts", "responses", "attention_mask"
107	
108	    Returns:
109	        tensor: sliced response tensor of shape [bsz, max_response_len, *]
110	    """
111	    values = tensor.values() if tensor.is_nested else tensor
112	    prompt_ids = data["prompts"]
113	    response_ids = data["responses"]
114	
115	    max_response_len = tu.get_non_tensor_data(data=data, key="max_response_len", default=-1)
116	
117	    if prompt_ids.is_nested:
118	        prompt_lens = prompt_ids.offsets().diff()
119	        response_lens = response_ids.offsets().diff()
120	        if max_response_len < 0:
121	            max_response_len = response_lens.max().item()
122	    else:
123	        attention_mask = data["attention_mask"]
124	        assert not attention_mask.is_nested
125	        prompt_lens = attention_mask[:, : prompt_ids.shape[1]].sum(dim=1)
126	        response_lens = attention_mask[:, prompt_ids.shape[1] :].sum(dim=1)
127	        max_response_len = response_ids.shape[1]
128	
129	    sequence_lens = prompt_lens + response_lens
130	    sequence_offsets = sequence_lens.cumsum(dim=0)
131	    assert sequence_offsets[-1].item() == values.shape[0]
132	    assert not prompt_lens.eq(0).any(), f"seq_offset - resp_len - 1 assumes prompt_len > 0. Got {prompt_lens}"
133	
134	    response_list = []
135	    # Skip padding dimensions after sequence dimensions, if any.
136	    skip_padding = (0, 0) * (values.ndim - 1)
137	    for resp_len, seq_offset in zip(response_lens, sequence_offsets, strict=True):
138	        pad_size = max_response_len - resp_len
139	        # left-shift model output by one token for log_probs/values
140	        response_list.append(F.pad(values[seq_offset - resp_len - 1 : seq_offset - 1], (*skip_padding, 0, pad_size)))
141	
142	    output = torch.stack(response_list, dim=0)
143	    return output
144

146	def build_attention_mask_from_nested(input_ids: torch.Tensor, max_seq_len: int | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
147	    """Build a padded full-sequence attention mask from nested input ids."""
148	    assert input_ids.is_nested, "input_ids must be a nested tensor"
149	    device = input_ids.values().device
150	    seq_lens = input_ids.offsets().diff().to(device=device)
151	    if max_seq_len is None:
152	        max_seq_len = int(seq_lens.max().item())
153	    positions = torch.arange(max_seq_len, device=device).unsqueeze(0)
154	    return (positions < seq_lens.unsqueeze(1)).to(torch.int32)

157	def embeds_padding_2_no_padding(data: TensorDict) -> TensorDict:
158	    """
159	    Convert TensorDict from prompt embeds with padding to no-padding format.
160	
161	    Currently we expect the prompt embedding mask to be [1111000...] format,
162	    which means the valid tokens are continuous and start from the left.
163	
164	    Args:
165	        data: TensorDict with "prompt_embeds", "prompt_embeds_mask",
166	              "negative_prompt_embeds", "negative_prompt_embeds_mask"
167	
168	    Returns:
169	        data: TensorDict with
170	        - Tensor includes NestedTensors "prompt_embeds", "prompt_embeds_mask",
171	          "negative_prompt_embeds", "negative_prompt_embeds_mask"
172	    """
173	
174	    def _to_nested(embeds: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor):
175	        """Strip padding from (bs, seq_len, dim) embeds using the boolean mask and return nested tensors."""
176	        embeds_list, mask_list = [], []
177	        for i in range(mask.shape[0]):
178	            curr_mask = mask[i].bool()
179	            embeds_list.append(embeds[i, curr_mask, :])
180	            mask_list.append(curr_mask[curr_mask])
181	        return (
182	            torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(embeds_list, layout=torch.jagged),
183	            torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(mask_list, layout=torch.jagged),
184	        )
185	
186	    data["prompt_embeds"], data["prompt_embeds_mask"] = _to_nested(data["prompt_embeds"], data["prompt_embeds_mask"])
187	
188	    if isinstance(data.get("negative_prompt_embeds", None), torch.Tensor):
189	        data["negative_prompt_embeds"], data["negative_prompt_embeds_mask"] = _to_nested(
190	            data["negative_prompt_embeds"], data["negative_prompt_embeds_mask"]
191	        )
192	
193	    return data

196	def response_from_nested(tensor: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
197	    """Extract response from nested model output.
198	
199	    Args:
200	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, prompt_len + response_len)
201	        response_mask: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
202	
203	    Returns:
204	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
205	    """
206	    values, offsets = tensor.values(), tensor.offsets()
207	    response_lens = response_mask.offsets().diff()
208	    response_list = []
209	    for resp_len, seq_offset in zip(response_lens, offsets[1:], strict=True):
210	        # left-shift model output by one token for log_probs/values
211	        response_list.append(values[seq_offset - resp_len - 1 : seq_offset - 1])
212	    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(response_list, layout=torch.jagged)

215	def response_to_nested(tensor: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
216	    """Convert padded response tensor to nested tensor.
217	
218	    Args:
219	        tensor: a tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
220	        response_mask: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
221	
222	    Returns:
223	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
224	    """
225	    assert response_mask.is_nested
226	    response_lens = response_mask.offsets().diff()
227	    response_list = []
228	    for i in range(tensor.shape[0]):
229	        response_list.append(tensor[i, : response_lens[i]])
230	
231	    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(response_list, layout=torch.jagged)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from omegaconf import DictConfig

    from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager.base import RawRewardFn, RewardManagerBase
    from verl.trainer.config.config import ModuleConfig
    from verl.workers.config.reward import RewardManagerConfig


def _call_with_kwargs(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.

    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
    """
    merged_kwargs = {**kwargs, **extra_kwargs}
    return raw_fn(*args, **merged_kwargs)


async def _call_with_kwargs_async(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.

    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
    """
    merged_kwargs = {**kwargs, **extra_kwargs}
    return await raw_fn(*args, **merged_kwargs)


def get_custom_reward_fn(config: DictConfig) -> Optional[RawRewardFn]:
    """Load and return a custom reward function from external file.

    Dynamically imports a reward function from a specified file path and wraps
    it with additional keyword arguments from the configuration.

    Args:
        config (dict): Configuration dictionary containing custom_reward_function
                      settings with 'path', 'name', and 'reward_kwargs' fields.

    Returns:
        callable or None: Wrapped reward function with merged kwargs, or None
                         if no custom reward function is configured.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the specified reward function file doesn't exist.
        RuntimeError: If there's an error loading the module from file.
        AttributeError: If the specified function name isn't found in the module.
    """

    reward_fn_config = config.reward.get("custom_reward_function") or {}
    module_path = reward_fn_config.get("path")
    if not module_path:
        return None

    fn_name = reward_fn_config.get("name")
    assert fn_name is not None

    from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_object

    raw_fn = load_extern_object(module_path=module_path, object_name=fn_name)

    reward_kwargs = dict(reward_fn_config.get("reward_kwargs", {}))
    if not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(raw_fn):
        return partial(_call_with_kwargs, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)
    else:
        return partial(_call_with_kwargs_async, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)


def resolve_reward_manager_cls(config: DictConfig) -> type[RewardManagerBase]:
    """Resolve the reward manager class from ``config`` without instantiating it."""
    reward_manager_cfg: RewardManagerConfig = config.reward.reward_manager
    if reward_manager_cfg.source == "register":
        from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager import get_reward_manager_cls

        return get_reward_manager_cls(reward_manager_cfg.name)
    elif reward_manager_cfg.source == "importlib":
        from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_object

        module_cfg: ModuleConfig | None = reward_manager_cfg.module
        assert module_cfg is not None and module_cfg.path is not None, (
            f"Module path is required when {reward_manager_cfg.source=}, but got {module_cfg=}"
        )
        return cast(
            "type[RewardManagerBase]",
            load_extern_object(module_path=module_cfg.path, object_name=reward_manager_cfg.name),
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown reward manager source: {reward_manager_cfg.source}")


def load_reward_manager(config: DictConfig, tokenizer: Any, **reward_kwargs: Any) -> RewardManagerBase:
    """
    Load and initialize a reward manager based on the configuration.

    Args:
        config: PPO trainer configuration object containing reward_model fields.
        tokenizer: Tokenizer object used for processing text.
        **reward_kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the reward manager.

    Returns:
        An instance of the specified reward manager class.
    """

    # Try to get a custom reward function based on the configuration
    # user defined reward manager can be registered in custom_reward_fn
    compute_score = get_custom_reward_fn(config)
    final_compute_score = compute_score

    reward_manager_cfg: RewardManagerConfig = config.reward.reward_manager
    reward_manager_cls = resolve_reward_manager_cls(config)

    default_compute_score_ = get_default_compute_score(reward_manager_cfg.name)

    if compute_score is None:
        sandbox_config = config.reward.get("sandbox_fusion")
        sandbox_url = sandbox_config.get("url") if sandbox_config else None
        memory_limit_mb = sandbox_config.get("memory_limit_mb", 1024) if sandbox_config else 1024
        if sandbox_url:
            sandbox_manager = multiprocessing.Manager()
            # Create a semaphore to control concurrent access to the sandbox
            _concurrent_semaphore = sandbox_manager.Semaphore(sandbox_config.get("max_concurrent", 64))
            final_compute_score = partial(
                default_compute_score_,
                sandbox_fusion_url=sandbox_url,
                concurrent_semaphore=_concurrent_semaphore,
                memory_limit_mb=memory_limit_mb,
            )
        else:
            final_compute_score = default_compute_score_

    # Instantiate and return the reward manager with the specified parameters
    return reward_manager_cls(
        config=config,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        compute_score=final_compute_score,
        **reward_kwargs,
    )


def extract_reward(batch: DataProto):
    """
    Extract reward tensor and extra info from batch data.
    """
    reward_tensor = batch.batch["rm_scores"]
    reward_extra_keys = batch.meta_info.get("reward_extra_keys", [])
    reward_extra_infos_dict = {key: batch.non_tensor_batch[key] for key in reward_extra_keys}
    return reward_tensor, reward_extra_infos_dict

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import os
import threading
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional

from verl.utils.import_utils import deprecated

# data_source -> sealed file relative to BENCH_BASELINE_REWARD_ROOT (/hidden/baseline)
_BASELINE_SCORE_REL: dict[str, str] = {
    "openai/gsm8k": "verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py",
}
_BASELINE_FN_CACHE: dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {}
_BASELINE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_BASELINE_WARNED = False


def _baseline_reward_root() -> str:
    """Sealed baseline root (Agent-invisible: /hidden or host hidden/baseline)."""
    env = (os.environ.get("BENCH_BASELINE_REWARD_ROOT") or "").strip()
    if env and os.path.isdir(env):
        return env
    # Docker verify mount (see DockerEnv.mount_hidden)
    if os.path.isdir("/hidden/baseline"):
        return "/hidden/baseline"
    return ""


def _load_baseline_compute_score(rel_path: str) -> Optional[Callable[..., Any]]:
    """Load compute_score from sealed baseline via importlib (not workspace package)."""
    root = _baseline_reward_root()
    if not root:
        return None
    path = os.path.join(root, rel_path.replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/"))
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None
    with _BASELINE_LOCK:
        cached = _BASELINE_FN_CACHE.get(path)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        mod_name = "_bench_sealed_reward_" + str(abs(hash(path)))
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(mod_name, path)
        if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
            return None
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
        fn = getattr(mod, "compute_score", None)
        if fn is None:
            return None
        _BASELINE_FN_CACHE[path] = fn
        return fn


def _is_validate(extra_info) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(extra_info, dict):
        return False
    return bool(extra_info.get("validate"))


def _try_baseline_score(data_source: str, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info):
    """If validate=True and sealed scorer exists, return score; else None."""
    global _BASELINE_WARNED
    if not _is_validate(extra_info):
        return None
    rel = _BASELINE_SCORE_REL.get(data_source)
    if not rel:
        return None
    fn = _load_baseline_compute_score(rel)
    if fn is None:
        if not _BASELINE_WARNED:
            _BASELINE_WARNED = True
            print(
                "[bench] WARN: validate=True but sealed baseline scorer missing "
                f"for {data_source=} (BENCH_BASELINE_REWARD_ROOT="
                f"{os.environ.get('BENCH_BASELINE_REWARD_ROOT', '')!r}); "
                "falling back to workspace scorer (val-core may be polluted).",
                flush=True,
            )
        return None
    return fn(solution_str, ground_truth)


def default_compute_score(
    data_source,
    solution_str,
    ground_truth,
    extra_info=None,
    sandbox_fusion_url=None,
    concurrent_semaphore=None,
    memory_limit_mb=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Compute the score for a given solution based on the data source.

    Args:
        data_source (str): The source dataset identifier which determines the scoring method.
        solution_str (str): The solution string to be evaluated.
        ground_truth (str): The ground truth answer for comparison.
        extra_info (dict, optional): Additional information that might be needed for scoring. Defaults to None.

    Returns:
        float: The computed score as a floating point number. If the result is a dictionary,
               it returns the dictionary instead.

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If the reward function is not implemented for the given data source.
    """
    baseline_res = _try_baseline_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info)
    if baseline_res is not None:
        res = baseline_res
    elif data_source == "openai/gsm8k":
        from . import gsm8k

        res = gsm8k.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
    elif data_source in ["lighteval/MATH", "DigitalLearningGmbH/MATH-lighteval", "HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500"]:
        from . import math_reward

        res = math_reward.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
        # [Optional] Math-Verify Integration
        # For enhanced accuracy, consider utilizing Math-Verify (https://github.com/huggingface/Math-Verify).
        # Note: Math-Verify needs to be manually installed via pip: `pip install math-verify`.
        # To use it, override the `compute_score` function with the following implementation:

        # from . import math_verify
        # res = math_verify.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
    elif data_source in ["math_dapo", "math", "math_dapo_reasoning"] or data_source.startswith("aime"):
        from . import math_dapo

        res = math_dapo.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
    elif data_source in [
        "numina_aops_forum",
        "numina_synthetic_math",
        "numina_amc_aime",
        "numina_synthetic_amc",
        "numina_cn_k12",
        "numina_olympiads",
    ]:
        from . import prime_math

        res = prime_math.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
    elif data_source == "taco":
        from . import taco

        res = taco.compute_score(
            solution_str=solution_str, ground_truth=ground_truth, extra_info=extra_info
        )
    elif data_source in ["codecontests", "apps", "codeforces"]:
        # Use the passed sandbox_fusion_url if available
        if sandbox_fusion_url:
            from . import sandbox_fusion

            # Pass the URL directly, ground_truth likely contains test cases here
            res = sandbox_fusion.compute_score(
                sandbox_fusion_url, concurrent_semaphore, memory_limit_mb, solution_str, ground_truth, continuous=True
            )
        else:
            # If no sandbox URL is provided, fall back to prime_code or raise error
            from . import prime_code

            # Assuming prime_code doesn't need the URL
            res = prime_code.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, continuous=True)
    elif data_source in ["hiyouga/geometry3k"]:
        from . import geo3k

        res = geo3k.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)
    elif data_source in [
        "searchR1_nq",
        "searchR1_triviaqa",
        "searchR1_popqa",
        "searchR1_hotpotqa",
        "searchR1_2wikimultihopqa",
        "searchR1_musique",
        "searchR1_bamboogle",
    ]:
        from . import search_r1_like_qa_em

        res = search_r1_like_qa_em.compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth)

    else:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"Reward function is not implemented for {data_source=}")

    if isinstance(res, dict):
        return res
    elif isinstance(res, int | float | bool):
        return float(res)
    else:
        return float(res[0])


@deprecated("verl.utils.reward_score.default_compute_score")
def _default_compute_score(
    data_source,
    solution_str,
    ground_truth,
    extra_info=None,
    sandbox_fusion_url=None,
    concurrent_semaphore=None,
    memory_limit_mb=None,
):
    """
    Legacy function API to be deprecated. Please use `default_compute_score` instead.
    """
    return default_compute_score(
        data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info, sandbox_fusion_url, concurrent_semaphore, memory_limit_mb
    )


def get_default_compute_score(reward_name: str | None):
    """Get the default compute_score function based on the reward manager type."""
    return default_compute_score


__all__ = ["default_compute_score"]

95	    RewardLoopWork can tackle reward computation:
96	    (1) rule-based reward computation

100	    Reward Computation Logic:
101	    - if user-customized reward function is provided:
102	        -> directly use user-customized reward function
103	    - if user-customized reward function is not provided:
104	        -> rm is not enabled: use default rule-based reward function
105	        -> rm is disrm: compute reward score using disrm
106	        -> rm is genrm: raise error (user-costomized reward func must be provided)

109	    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, reward_router_address: str = None):

177	    async def compute_score(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
178	        if self.config.reward.custom_reward_function.path is not None:
179	            # directly use user-customized reward function
180	            return await self.reward_manager.run_single(data)
181	        else:

183	                # we assume the rm is disrm

189	    async def _post_request(self, payload: dict, endpoint: str, max_retries: int = 16):
190	        url = f"http://{self.reward_router_address}/{endpoint}"
191	        last_exception = None
192	        for attempt in range(max_retries):
193	            try:
194	                # It's safer to have a timeout instead of None, which can hang indefinitely.
195	                timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None)
196	                async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as session:
197	                    async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
198	                        resp.raise_for_status()
199	                        return await resp.json()
200	            except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as e:
201	                # Do not retry on 4xx client errors, but retry on 5xx server errors.
202	                if 400 <= e.status < 500:
203	                    logger.error(f"Request to {url} failed with client error HTTP {e.status}: {e}. Not retrying.")
204	                    raise
205	                last_exception = e
206	                logger.warning(
207	                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with HTTP {e.status}: {e}. "
208	                    "Retrying..."
209	                )
210	            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, aiohttp.ClientConnectorError) as e:
211	                last_exception = e
212	                logger.warning(f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed: {e}. Retrying...")
213	            except Exception as e:
214	                last_exception = e
215	                logger.warning(
216	                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with unexpected error: {e}. "
217	                    "Retrying..."
218	                )
219	
220	            if attempt < max_retries - 1:
221	                # Using exponential backoff is generally better than a fixed sleep.
222	                backoff_seconds = 2**attempt
223	                await asyncio.sleep(min(backoff_seconds, 30))
224	
225	        logger.error(f"Max retries ({max_retries}) reached for request to {url}.")
226	        if last_exception:
227	            raise last_exception

229	    async def _preprocess_reward_inputs(self, data: DataProto) -> str:
230	        assert len(data) == 1, "RewardLoopWorker only support single data item"
231	        data_item = data[0]
232	        assert "raw_prompt" in data_item.non_tensor_batch
233	
234	        # extract raw prompt
235	        chat: list = list(data_item.non_tensor_batch["raw_prompt"])
236	
237	        # extract response
238	        response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
239	        response_length = response_ids.shape[-1]
240	        valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][-response_length:].sum()
241	        valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]
242	
243	        rollout_response = self.input_tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids)
244	        rollout_response = rollout_response.replace(self.input_tokenizer.eos_token, "")
245	
246	        chat.append({"role": "assistant", "content": rollout_response})
247	
248	        rm_prompt = self.reward_model_tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
249	            chat,
250	            add_generation_prompt=False,
251	            tokenize=False,
252	        )
253	
254	        # llama tokenizer will add bos token by default
255	        # will be removed in vllm >= 0.11.2, where we can add "add_special_tokens" = False
256	        if self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token is not None and rm_prompt.startswith(
257	            self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token
258	        ):
259	            rm_prompt = rm_prompt[len(self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token) :]
260	
261	        return rm_prompt
262	
263	    async def compute_score_disrm(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
264	        disrm_prompt = await self._preprocess_reward_inputs(data)
265	        engine_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.rollout.name
266	        model_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path
267	        if engine_name == "vllm":
268	            payloads = {
269	                "model": model_name,
270	                "input": disrm_prompt,
271	                "use_activation": False,
272	            }
273	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "classify")
274	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["probs"][-1]
275	        elif engine_name == "sglang":
276	            payloads = {
277	                "model": model_name,
278	                "input": disrm_prompt,
279	            }
280	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/embeddings")
281	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["embedding"][-1]
282	        elif engine_name == "trtllm":
283	            # TODO: remove this once TRT-LLM switches to TorchSampler
284	            raise ValueError("TensorRT-LLM backend does not support reward models currently.")
285	
286	            payloads = {
287	                "model": model_name,
288	                "prompt": disrm_prompt,
289	                "return_context_logits": True,
290	            }
291	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/completions")
292	            rm_score = output["choices"][0]["context_logits"]
293	            assert isinstance(rm_score, list) and len(rm_score) > 0, (
294	                "TensorRT-LLM OpenAI server response for reward score is not in the expected format."
295	            )
296	
297	            rm_score = float(rm_score[0][0])
298	            logger.debug(f"rm score: {rm_score}")
299	        else:
300	            raise NotImplementedError(f"RewardLoopManager does not support {engine_name}")
301	
302	        return {"reward_score": rm_score}

305	class RewardLoopManager:
306	    """
307	    RewardLoopManager run in single controller.
308	    This class will create reward loop workers and manage them.
309	    """
310	
311	    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, rm_resource_pool: RayResourcePool = None):
312	        self.config = config
313	        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
314	            self.reward_model_manager = RewardModelManager(config.reward.reward_model, rm_resource_pool)
315	            self.reward_router_address = self.reward_model_manager.get_router_address()
316	        else:
317	            self.reward_model_manager = None
318	            self.reward_router_address = None
319	
320	        self.reward_loop_workers_class = ray.remote(RewardLoopWorker)
321	        self.reward_manager_cls = resolve_reward_manager_cls(config)
322	        self._init_reward_loop_workers()
323	
324	    @property
325	    def reward_loop_worker_handles(self) -> list[ActorHandle]:
326	        """Return worker handles for agent loop worker to compute reward score.
327	
328	        Only return worker handles when reward computation can be parallelized with rollout:
329	        (1) rule-based reward without reward model
330	        (2) reward model with extra resource pool
331	        """
332	        if not self.config.reward.reward_model.enable or self.config.reward.reward_model.enable_resource_pool:
333	            return self.reward_loop_workers
334	        return None
335	
336	    def _init_reward_loop_workers(self):
337	        self.reward_loop_workers = []
338	        num_workers = self.config.reward.num_workers
339	        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]
340	
341	        for i in range(num_workers):
342	            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
343	            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]
344	
345	            self.reward_loop_workers.append(
346	                self.reward_loop_workers_class.options(
347	                    name=f"reward_loop_worker_{i}",
348	                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
349	                        node_id=node_id,
350	                        soft=True,
351	                    ),
352	                ).remote(self.config, self.reward_router_address)
353	            )
354	
355	    def compute_rm_score(self, data: DataProto) -> DataProto:
356	        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
357	            self.reward_model_manager.wake_up()
358	
359	        num_workers = len(self.reward_loop_workers)
360	        padded_data, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(data, num_workers)
361	        chunks = padded_data.chunk(num_workers)
362	        outputs = ray.get(
363	            [
364	                worker.compute_score_batch.remote(chunk)
365	                for worker, chunk in zip(self.reward_loop_workers, chunks, strict=True)
366	            ]
367	        )
368	        outputs_flat = [item for sublist in outputs for item in sublist]
369	        if pad_size > 0:
370	            outputs_flat = outputs_flat[: len(data)]
371	
372	        # compute rm score
373	        scores = [item["reward_score"] for item in outputs_flat]
374	        rm_scores = self.reward_manager_cls.assemble_rm_scores(data, scores)
375	        batch = TensorDict({"rm_scores": rm_scores}, batch_size=len(data))
376	
377	        reward_extra_infos = [output.get("reward_extra_info", {}) for output in outputs_flat]
378	        reward_extra_keys = list(reward_extra_infos[0].keys())
379	        non_tensor_batch = {}
380	        for key in reward_extra_keys:
381	            non_tensor_batch[key] = np.array([info[key] for info in reward_extra_infos], dtype=object)
382	
383	        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
384	            self.reward_model_manager.sleep()
385	
386	        return DataProto(
387	            batch=batch, non_tensor_batch=non_tensor_batch, meta_info={"reward_extra_keys": reward_extra_keys}
388	        )
389	
390	    def _run_all(self, tasks: list[asyncio.Task]):
391	        async def run_all():
392	            return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
393	
394	        return asyncio.run(run_all())

182	        metrics: dict = output.pop("metrics")
183	        # perform all gather in dp group to ensure that it's correct.

185	        # we should always sum the loss of each micro-batch as we scale by global_bsz/global_token
186	        loss = torch.sum(torch.tensor(output.pop("loss"), device=self.device_name))

201	        else:

206	        if lr is not None:

import inspect

from verl import DataProto
from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager import register
from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager.base import RewardManagerBase
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score


@register("naive")
class NaiveRewardManager(RewardManagerBase):
    """The reward manager."""

    def __init__(self, config, tokenizer, compute_score, reward_router_address=None, reward_model_tokenizer=None):
        super().__init__(config, tokenizer, compute_score)
        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
        self.is_async_reward_score = inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.compute_score)
        self.reward_router_address = reward_router_address
        self.reward_model_tokenizer = reward_model_tokenizer

    async def run_single(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
        data = data[-1:]  # for multi-sequence outputs, we only compute reward based on the last sequence
        data_item = data[0]
        response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
        response_length = response_ids.shape[-1]
        valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][-response_length:].sum()
        valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

        data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch["data_source"]
        ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["ground_truth"]
        extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("extra_info", {})
        if not isinstance(extra_info, dict):
            extra_info = {}
        else:
            extra_info = dict(extra_info)
        tool_extra_fields = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("tool_extra_fields", None)
        if tool_extra_fields is not None:
            extra_info.update(tool_extra_fields.items())

        num_turns = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("__num_turns__", None)
        rollout_reward_scores = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_scores", {})
        extra_info["num_turns"] = num_turns
        extra_info["rollout_reward_scores"] = rollout_reward_scores
        # Bench: propagate validate flag so default_compute_score can use sealed baseline.
        if bool(data.meta_info.get("validate", False)):
            extra_info["validate"] = True

        response_str = await self.loop.run_in_executor(
            None, lambda: self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)
        )

        extra_reward_kwargs = (
            {
                "reward_router_address": self.reward_router_address,
                "reward_model_tokenizer": self.reward_model_tokenizer,
            }
            if self.reward_router_address is not None
            else {}
        )
        if self.is_async_reward_score:
            result = await self.compute_score(
                data_source=data_source,
                solution_str=response_str,
                ground_truth=ground_truth,
                extra_info=extra_info,
                **extra_reward_kwargs,
            )
        else:
            result = await self.loop.run_in_executor(
                None,
                lambda: self.compute_score(
                    data_source=data_source,
                    solution_str=response_str,
                    ground_truth=ground_truth,
                    extra_info=extra_info,
                    **extra_reward_kwargs,
                ),
            )

        reward_extra_info = {}

        score: float
        if isinstance(result, dict):
            score = result["score"]
            for key, value in result.items():
                reward_extra_info[key] = value
        else:
            score = result
            reward_extra_info["acc"] = score

        reward = score

        return {"reward_score": reward, "reward_extra_info": reward_extra_info}

import logging
import os
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Any, Callable

import torch
from omegaconf import DictConfig
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.ray_utils import get_event_loop

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)
logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))


RawRewardFn = Callable[..., Any] | None


class RewardManagerBase(ABC):
    _class_initialized = False

    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, tokenizer: AutoTokenizer, compute_score: RawRewardFn):
        """Initialize reward manager.

        Args:
            config (DictConfig): YAML config.
            tokenizer (AutoTokenizer): Tokenizer for tokenize messages.
        """
        self.config = config
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.compute_score = compute_score
        self.loop = get_event_loop()
        self.init_class(config, tokenizer)

    @classmethod
    def init_class(cls, config: DictConfig, tokenizer: AutoTokenizer):
        """Initialize class state shared across all instances."""
        if cls._class_initialized:
            return
        cls._class_initialized = True

    @abstractmethod
    async def run_single(self, data: DataProto):
        raise NotImplementedError

    @classmethod
    def assemble_rm_scores(cls, data: DataProto, scores: list[float]) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Assemble per-sample reward scores into the ``rm_scores`` tensor for a batch.

        Args:
            data: The concatenated batch passed to :meth:`run_single`.
                ``data.batch["prompts"]``, ``data.batch["responses"]`` and
                ``data.batch["attention_mask"]`` are expected to be present
                for the default implementation.
            scores: List of scalar reward scores, one per sample in ``data``.

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: The ``rm_scores`` tensor with leading dimension equal to
            ``len(data)``.
        """
        prompt_length = data.batch["prompts"].size(1)
        valid_response_length = data.batch["attention_mask"][:, prompt_length:].sum(dim=1)
        rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
        rm_scores[torch.arange(rm_scores.size(0), device=rm_scores.device), valid_response_length - 1] = (
            rm_scores.new_tensor(scores)
        )
        return rm_scores

689	    def optimizer_step(self):

695	        """
696	        assert self.optimizer_config.clip_grad is not None
697	
698	        # getattr fallback: some subclasses (e.g. VeOmniEngine) bypass FSDPEngine.__init__.
699	        scaler = getattr(self, "scaler", None)
700	
701	        # Unscale gradients before clip so the clip threshold is applied to true gradient
702	        # magnitudes, not scaled ones. scaler.step() will skip the update if any grad is inf/nan.
703	        if scaler is not None:
704	            scaler.unscale_(self.optimizer)
705	
706	        if isinstance(self.module, FSDP):
707	            grad_norm = self.module.clip_grad_norm_(self.optimizer_config.clip_grad)
708	        elif isinstance(self.module, FSDPModule):
709	            grad_norm = fsdp2_clip_grad_norm_(self.module.parameters(), max_norm=self.optimizer_config.clip_grad)
710	        else:

712	                self.module.parameters(), max_norm=self.optimizer_config.clip_grad
713	            )
714	
715	        if isinstance(grad_norm, DTensor):
716	            grad_norm = grad_norm.full_tensor()
717	
718	        if scaler is not None:
719	            # scaler handles inf/nan skipping internally via _check_inf_per_device.
720	            scaler.step(self.optimizer)
721	            scaler.update()
722	        else:
723	            # if grad_norm is not finite, skip the update
724	            if not torch.isfinite(grad_norm):
725	                print(f"WARN: grad_norm is not finite: {grad_norm}")

727	            else:
728	                self.optimizer.step()

732	
733	            invalidate_all_scales(self.module)

735	        return grad_norm.item()

245	        if self.disable_auto_offload:

249	                return

251	            self.engine.to(device=device, model=self.engine.is_param_offload_enabled, optimizer=False, grad=False)
252	        elif self.mode == "train":
253	            self.engine.to(
254	                device=device,
255	                model=self.engine.is_param_offload_enabled,
256	                optimizer=self.engine.is_optimizer_offload_enabled,
257	                grad=self.engine.is_param_offload_enabled,
258	            )

262	        self._context_switch(get_device_name())

269	class EngineRegistry:
270	    """
271	    A registry for managing and instantiating different types of training engines.
272	
273	    This class uses a dictionary to store engine classes, mapping a string key to each class.
274	    It provides a decorator `register` to add new engines to the registry and a `new` method
275	    to create an instance of a registered engine.
276	    """
277	
278	    _engines = {}
279	
280	    @classmethod
281	    def register(
282	        cls,
283	        model_type: str,
284	        backend: list[str] | str,
285	        device: list[str] | str = "cuda",
286	        vendor: list[str] | str | None = None,
287	    ):
288	        """
289	        A class method decorator that registers an engine class with a given key.
290	
291	        This allows for dynamic instantiation of engine classes by their registered key.
292	
293	        Args:
294	            model_type (str): The type of the model
295	            backend (list[str] | str): The backend to use for the model type
296	            device (list[str] | str): The device type (e.g., "cuda", "npu", "cpu") this engine supports,
297	                default is "cuda"
298	            vendor (list[str] | str | None): The hardware vendor (e.g., "nvidia", "metax") this engine
299	                supports. If None, the engine is registered as the default for the device type.
300	
301	        Returns:
302	            A decorator function that takes an engine class and registers it.
303	        """
304	
305	        def decorator(engine_class):
306	            assert issubclass(engine_class, BaseEngine)
307	            if model_type not in cls._engines:
308	                cls._engines[model_type] = {}
309	
310	            backends = backend if isinstance(backend, list) else [backend]
311	            devices = device if isinstance(device, list) else [device]
312	            vendors = vendor if isinstance(vendor, list) else ([vendor] if vendor else [None])
313	            for current_backend in backends:
314	                for current_device in devices:
315	                    if current_backend not in cls._engines[model_type]:
316	                        cls._engines[model_type][current_backend] = {}
317	                    for current_vendor in vendors:
318	                        key = (current_device, current_vendor) if current_vendor else current_device
319	                        assert key not in cls._engines[model_type][current_backend], (
320	                            f"The key(device-vendor: {key}) has been already registed!"
321	                        )
322	                        cls._engines[model_type][current_backend][key] = engine_class
323	
324	            return engine_class
325	
326	        return decorator
327	
328	    @classmethod
329	    def get_engine_cls(cls, model_type: str, backend: str):
330	        assert model_type in cls._engines, f"Unknown model_type: {model_type}"
331	        assert backend in cls._engines[model_type], f"Unknown backend: {backend}"
332	        device = get_device_name()
333	        vendor = get_vendor()
334	        # Allow environment variables to override detected device and vendor for engine selection, if set
335	        if os.getenv("VERL_ENGINE_DEVICE"):
336	            device = os.getenv("VERL_ENGINE_DEVICE")
337	        if os.getenv("VERL_ENGINE_VENDOR"):
338	            vendor = os.getenv("VERL_ENGINE_VENDOR")
339	        registry = cls._engines[model_type][backend]
340	
341	        # Try vendor-specific lookup: (device, vendor)
342	        vendor_key = (device, vendor)
343	        if vendor_key in registry:
344	            return registry[vendor_key]
345	
346	        # Fallback to device-only key (registered without vendor)
347	        if device in registry:
348	            return registry[device]
349	
350	        # For cuda-compatible vendors without a specific registration, try nvidia
351	        if device == "cuda" and vendor != "nvidia":
352	            nvidia_key = (device, "nvidia")
353	            if nvidia_key in registry:
354	                return registry[nvidia_key]
355	
356	        raise ValueError(
357	            f"No engine registered for device={device!r}, vendor={vendor!r}, "
358	            f"model_type={model_type!r}, backend={backend!r}"
359	        )
360	
361	    @classmethod
362	    def new(cls, model_type, backend, *args, **kwargs):
363	        """
364	        Function to create a new training engine instance based on the provided config.
365	        Args:
366	            key: A configuration object containing the engine key and other settings.
367	            *args: Variable length argument list.
368	            **kwargs: Arbitrary keyword arguments.
369	        Returns:
370	            engine: An instance of the training engine corresponding to the config.
371	        Raises:
372	            NotImplementedError: If the engine key in the config does not match any known engines.
373	        """
374	        engine_cls = cls.get_engine_cls(model_type, backend)
375	        return engine_cls(*args, **kwargs)

243	    """Build an optimizer based on the configuration.
244	
245	    Dynamically imports and instantiates an optimizer class from the specified module.
246	
247	    Args:
248	        parameters: Model parameters to optimize
249	        config: FSDPOptimizerConfig with optimizer settings
250	
251	    Returns:
252	        Optimizer instance
253	
254	    Examples:
255	        # PyTorch AdamW
256	        config.optimizer_impl = "torch.optim"
257	        config.optimizer = "AdamW"
258	
259	        # TorchAO AdamW with bf16 stochastic rounding
260	        config.optimizer_impl = "torchao.optim"
261	        config.optimizer = "_AdamW"
262	        config.override_optimizer_config = {"bf16_stochastic_round": True}
263	
264	        # BitsAndBytes AdamW 8bit
265	        config.optimizer_impl = "bitsandbytes.optim"
266	        config.optimizer = "AdamW8bit"
267	    """
268	    import importlib
269	
270	    optimizer_args = {
271	        "lr": config.lr,
272	        "weight_decay": config.weight_decay,
273	    }
274	
275	    optimizer_name_lower = config.optimizer.lower()
276	    if "adam" in optimizer_name_lower or "ademamix" in optimizer_name_lower:
277	        optimizer_args["betas"] = config.betas
278	
279	    if config.override_optimizer_config is not None:
280	        optimizer_args.update(config.override_optimizer_config)
281	
282	    try:
283	        module = importlib.import_module(config.optimizer_impl)
284	        optimizer_cls = getattr(module, config.optimizer)
285	    except ImportError as e:
286	        raise ImportError(
287	            f"Failed to import module '{config.optimizer_impl}'. Make sure the package is installed. Error: {e}"
288	        ) from e
289	    except AttributeError as e:
290	        raise AttributeError(
291	            f"Optimizer '{config.optimizer}' not found in module '{config.optimizer_impl}'. "
292	            f"Available optimizers: {dir(module)}"
293	        ) from e
294	
295	    return optimizer_cls(parameters, **optimizer_args)

49	def gather_from_labels(data: torch.Tensor, label: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
50	    """Gather values from data tensor at positions specified by label indices.
51	
52	    Selects elements from the last dimension of `data` based on indices in `label`.
53	    Commonly used to extract log-probabilities for specific token IDs from a
54	    vocabulary distribution.
55	
56	    Args:
57	        data: Input tensor of shape (..., vocab_size) containing values to gather from.
58	        label: Index tensor of shape (...,) with values in range [0, vocab_size).
59	
60	    Returns:
61	        torch.Tensor: Gathered values with shape (...,), same as label shape.
62	
63	    Example:
64	        >>> logits = torch.randn(2, 3, 100)  # [batch, seq, vocab]
65	        >>> labels = torch.randint(0, 100, (2, 3))  # [batch, seq]
66	        >>> gathered = gather_from_labels(logits, labels)  # [batch, seq]
67	    """
68	    output = torch.gather(data, -1, label.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
69	    return output

72	def logprobs_from_logits(logits, labels, inplace_backward=True):
73	    """
74	    Compute per-token log-probabilities for the given labels.
75	
76	    Uses a Flash-Attention–based cross-entropy (if available) for efficient backward,
77	    otherwise falls back to a standard log-softmax+gather approach.
78	
79	    See: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/563#issuecomment-330103591
80	
81	    Args:
82	        logits (Tensor): Model outputs of shape (..., vocab_size).
83	        labels (LongTensor): True class indices of shape matching logits[..., :-1].
84	        inplace_backward (bool): If True and Flash-Attn is available, perform backward in-place.
85	
86	    Returns:
87	        Tensor: Log-probabilities of the target labels, shape logits.shape[:-1].
88	    """
89	    if FLAH_ATTN_CROSS_ENTROPY_LOSS_AVAILABLE:
90	        batch_dim = logits.shape[:-1]
91	        last_dim = logits.shape[-1]
92	        logits = logits.reshape(-1, last_dim)
93	        labels = labels.reshape(-1)
94	        output = logprobs_from_logits_flash_attn(logits, labels, inplace_backward=inplace_backward)
95	        output = output.view(*batch_dim)
96	    elif NPU_CROSS_ENTROPY_LOSS_AVAILABLE:
97	        output = logprobs_from_logits_torch_npu(logits, labels)
98	    else:
99	        output = logprobs_from_logits_v2(logits, labels)

166	def logprobs_from_logits_v2(logits: torch.FloatTensor, labels: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
167	    """Memory-efficient log-probability computation using row-wise processing.
168	
169	    Computes log-probabilities by processing one row at a time to reduce peak
170	    memory consumption. Uses logsumexp for float32/float64, falls back to
171	    log_softmax for bfloat16 due to numerical stability concerns.
172	
173	    The mathematical identity used is: log_softmax(x_i) = x_i - logsumexp(x)
174	
175	    Args:
176	        logits: Model output logits of shape (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
177	            or (batch_size, vocab_size).
178	        labels: Target token indices matching logits shape without vocab dimension.
179	
180	    Returns:
181	        torch.Tensor: Log-probabilities for target labels.
182	
183	    Note:
184	        This implementation trades compute for memory by iterating over batch
185	        dimension, making it suitable for large vocabulary sizes.
186	    """
187	    if logits.dtype in [torch.float32, torch.float64]:
188	        logits_labels = torch.gather(logits, dim=-1, index=labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
189	        # loop to reduce peak mem consumption
190	        logsumexp_values = torch.stack([torch.logsumexp(logit, dim=-1) for logit in logits])
191	        logprobs_labels = logits_labels - logsumexp_values  # log_softmax(x_i) = x_i - logsumexp(x)
192	    else:
193	        # logsumexp approach is unstable with bfloat16, fall back to slightly less efficent approach
194	        logprobs_labels = []
195	        for row_logits, row_labels in zip(logits, labels, strict=True):  # loop to reduce peak mem consumption
196	            row_logprobs = F.log_softmax(row_logits, dim=-1)
197	            row_logprobs_labels = row_logprobs.gather(dim=-1, index=row_labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
198	            logprobs_labels.append(row_logprobs_labels)
199	        logprobs_labels = torch.stack(logprobs_labels)
200	    return logprobs_labels

203	def clip_by_value(x: torch.Tensor, tensor_min: torch.Tensor, tensor_max: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
204	    """Clip tensor values to a range defined by tensor bounds.
205	
206	    Extension of torch.clamp that supports tensor-valued min/max bounds
207	    instead of only scalar bounds.
208	
209	    Args:
210	        x: Input tensor to clip.
211	        tensor_min: Minimum bound tensor (broadcastable to x).
212	        tensor_max: Maximum bound tensor (broadcastable to x).
213

216	
217	    See Also:
218	        https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/2793#issuecomment-428784713
219	    """

224	def entropy_from_logits(logits: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
225	    """Calculate Shannon entropy from unnormalized logits.
226	
227	    Computes H(p) = -sum(p * log(p)) using the numerically stable formula:
228	    entropy = logsumexp(logits) - sum(softmax(logits) * logits)
229	
230	    Args:
231	        logits: Unnormalized log-probabilities of shape (..., vocab_size).
232	
233	    Returns:
234	        torch.Tensor: Entropy values with shape (...,), one per distribution.
235	    """
236	    pd = torch.nn.functional.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
237	    entropy = torch.logsumexp(logits, dim=-1) - torch.sum(pd * logits, dim=-1)
238	    return entropy

241	def entropy_from_logits_with_chunking(logits: torch.Tensor, chunk_size: int = 2048) -> torch.Tensor:
242	    """Memory-efficient entropy calculation using chunked processing.
243	
244	    Computes entropy by processing the batch in chunks to reduce peak memory
245	    usage. Useful for large batch sizes or when memory is constrained.
246	
247	    Args:
248	        logits: Unnormalized log-probabilities of shape (batch_size, vocab_size).
249	        chunk_size: Number of samples to process at once. Defaults to 2048.
250	
251	    Returns:
252	        torch.Tensor: Entropy values with shape (batch_size,).
253	
254	    Note:
255	        Converts chunks to float32 for numerical stability during computation.
256	    """
257	    entropy = torch.zeros(logits.shape[0], device=logits.device)
258	    for i in range(0, logits.shape[0], chunk_size):
259	        logits_chunk = logits[i : i + chunk_size].float()
260	        pd_chunk = torch.nn.functional.softmax(logits_chunk, dim=-1)
261	        entropy_chunk = torch.logsumexp(logits_chunk, dim=-1) - torch.sum(pd_chunk * logits_chunk, dim=-1)
262	        entropy[i : i + chunk_size] = entropy_chunk
263	    return entropy

266	def masked_sum(values: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor, axis: int | tuple[int, ...] | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
267	    """Compute sum of tensor values where mask is True.
268	
269	    NaN values outside the mask are replaced with zeros to prevent
270	    contaminating the sum.
271	
272	    Args:
273	        values: Input tensor containing values to sum.
274	        mask: Boolean or numeric mask tensor (same shape as values).
275	            Non-zero values indicate elements to include.
276	        axis: Dimension(s) along which to sum. None sums all elements.
277	
278	    Returns:
279	        torch.Tensor: Sum of masked values, reduced along specified axis.
280	    """
281	    # If NaNs exist out of mask, replace NaNs in values with a value that
282	    # won't affect the sum (e.g., 0 for masked regions)
283	    valid_values = torch.where(mask.bool(), values, 0.0)
284	    return (valid_values * mask).sum(axis=axis)
285	
286	
287	def masked_mean(values, mask, axis=None):
288	    """
289	    Compute the mean of `values` over elements selected by `mask`.
290	
291	    Args:
292	        values (Tensor): Input tensor.
293	        mask (Tensor): Boolean or numeric mask of the same shape as `values`.
294	        axis (int or tuple of int, optional): Dimension(s) along which to compute the mean.
295	            Defaults to None (over all elements).
296	
297	    Returns:
298	        Tensor: Masked mean, with shape equal to `values` reduced over `axis`.
299	    """
300	    s = masked_sum(values, mask, axis)
301	    return s / (mask.sum(axis=axis) + 1e-8)
302	
303	
304	def masked_var(values, mask, unbiased=True):
305	    """Compute variance of tensor with masked values."""
306	    mean = masked_mean(values, mask)
307	    centered_values = values - mean
308	    variance = masked_mean(centered_values**2, mask)
309	    if unbiased:
310	        mask_sum = mask.sum()
311	        if mask_sum == 0:
312	            raise ValueError("At least one element in the mask has to be 1.")
313	        # note that if mask_sum == 1, then there is a division by zero issue
314	        # to avoid it you just need to use a larger minibatch_size
315	        if mask_sum == 1:
316	            raise ValueError("The sum of the mask is one, which can cause a division by zero.")
317	        bessel_correction = mask_sum / (mask_sum - 1)
318	        variance = variance * bessel_correction
319	    return variance
320	
321	
322	def masked_whiten(values, mask, shift_mean=True):
323	    """
324	    Whiten `values` by normalizing with mean and variance computed over `mask`.
325	
326	    Args:
327	        values (torch.Tensor): Input tensor.
328	        mask (torch.Tensor): Boolean tensor of same shape, selects elements for stats.
329	        shift_mean (bool): If True (default), output is zero-mean;
330	                           if False, the original mean is re-added after scaling.
331	
332	    Returns:
333	        torch.Tensor: Whitened tensor of same shape as `values`.
334	    """
335	    mean, var = masked_mean(values, mask), masked_var(values, mask)
336	    whitened = (values - mean) * torch.rsqrt(var + 1e-8)
337	    if not shift_mean:
338	        whitened += mean
339	    return whitened

713	    zero_indexed_step: bool = True,
714	):
715	    """
716	    Create a schedule with a learning rate that decreases following the values of the cosine function between the
717	    initial lr set in the optimizer to 0, after a warmup period during which it increases linearly between 0 and the
718	    initial lr set in the optimizer.
719	    Args:
720	        optimizer (:class:`~torch.optim.Optimizer`):
721	            The optimizer for which to schedule the learning rate.
722	        num_warmup_steps (:obj:`int`):
723	            The number of steps for the warmup phase.

725	            The total number of training steps.

727	            The minimum lr ratio w.r.t the maximum.
728	        num_cycles (:obj:`float`, `optional`, defaults to 0.5):
729	            The number of waves in the cosine schedule (the defaults is to just decrease from the max value to 0
730	            following a half-cosine).
731	        last_epoch (:obj:`int`, `optional`, defaults to -1):
732	            The index of the last epoch when resuming training.
733	        init_lr_ratio (:obj:`float`, `optional`, defaults to None):
734	            The initial lr ratio w.r.t the maximum.
735	        zero_indexed_step (:obj:`bool`, `optional`, defaults to True):
736	            Whether the LR schedule uses 0-indexed steps. If True (default), step counting starts at 0.
737	            If False (used by torchtitan), step counting starts at 1.
738	    Return:
739	        :obj:`torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR` with the appropriate schedule.
740	    """
741	    min_lr_ratio = 0.0 if min_lr_ratio is None else min_lr_ratio
742	    assert min_lr_ratio >= 0 and min_lr_ratio <= 1.0
743	    coef = (1 - min_lr_ratio) * 0.5
744	    intercept = (1 + min_lr_ratio) * 0.5
745	
746	    init_lr_ratio = 0.0 if init_lr_ratio is None else init_lr_ratio
747	    assert init_lr_ratio >= 0 and init_lr_ratio <= 1.0
748	
749	    def lr_lambda(current_step):
750	        if not zero_indexed_step:
751	            current_step += 1
752	        if current_step < num_warmup_steps:
753	            return init_lr_ratio + (1.0 - init_lr_ratio) * (float(current_step) / float(max(1, num_warmup_steps)))
754	        progress = float(current_step - num_warmup_steps) / float(max(1, num_training_steps - num_warmup_steps))
755	        x = math.cos(math.pi * float(num_cycles) * 2.0 * progress)
756	        return max(min_lr_ratio, x * coef + intercept)
757	
758	    return LambdaLR(optimizer, lr_lambda, last_epoch)

762	    optimizer: Optimizer,

767	    Create a constant LR schedule with a linear warmup phase.
768	
769	    Args:
770	        optimizer (Optimizer): Wrapped optimizer.
771	        num_warmup_steps (int): Number of steps to ramp up the LR from 0 to initial value.

138	def compute_spec_decode_metrics(
139	    spec_drafts,
140	    spec_accepts,
141	    spec_verifies,
142	    non_padding_mask=None,
143	) -> dict:
144	    """Aggregate per-request speculative decoding stats.
145	
146	    Ratios are computed per request and then averaged, so long and short
147	    responses have equal metric weight.
148	
149	    The three inputs come from the rollout engine (vLLM request spec-decode
150	    stats or sglang ``meta_info["spec_*"]`` keys). Either all three are ``None``
151	    (caller didn't fetch them, e.g. spec rollout disabled) and the function
152	    is a no-op, or all three are populated; mixed state is a programmer error.
153	
154	    ``non_padding_mask`` is a numpy bool array used by sync PPO to drop padded
155	    placeholder samples; pass ``None`` for async PPO.
156	    """
157	    if spec_drafts is None and spec_accepts is None and spec_verifies is None:
158	        return {}
159	    assert spec_drafts is not None and spec_accepts is not None and spec_verifies is not None, (
160	        "spec_decode metrics require all three of spec_num_draft_tokens / "
161	        "spec_num_accepted_tokens / spec_num_verify_steps; got partial inputs"
162	    )
163	
164	    drafts = spec_drafts.tolist() if hasattr(spec_drafts, "tolist") else list(spec_drafts)
165	    accepts = spec_accepts.tolist() if hasattr(spec_accepts, "tolist") else list(spec_accepts)
166	    verifies = spec_verifies.tolist() if hasattr(spec_verifies, "tolist") else list(spec_verifies)
167	
168	    if non_padding_mask is not None:
169	        drafts = [d for d, keep in zip(drafts, non_padding_mask, strict=True) if keep]
170	        accepts = [a for a, keep in zip(accepts, non_padding_mask, strict=True) if keep]
171	        verifies = [v for v, keep in zip(verifies, non_padding_mask, strict=True) if keep]
172	
173	    if len(drafts) == 0:
174	        return {}
175	
176	    # Treat zero-denominator samples as 0.0 and keep them in the mean.
177	    per_sample_accept_rate = [(a / d) if d > 0 else 0.0 for a, d in zip(accepts, drafts, strict=True)]
178	    per_sample_accept_length = [(1.0 + a / v) if v > 0 else 0.0 for a, v in zip(accepts, verifies, strict=True)]
179	
180	    n = len(drafts)
181	    return {
182	        "rollout/spec_accept_rate": float(sum(per_sample_accept_rate) / n),
183	        "rollout/spec_accept_length": float(sum(per_sample_accept_length) / n),
184	    }

187	def compute_advantage(
188	    data: DataProto,
189	    adv_estimator: AdvantageEstimator,
190	    gamma: float = 1.0,
191	    lam: float = 1.0,
192	    num_repeat: int = 1,
193	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
194	    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
195	) -> DataProto:
196	    """Compute advantage estimates for policy optimization.
197	
198	    This function computes advantage estimates using various estimators like GAE, GRPO, REINFORCE++, etc.
199	    The advantage estimates are used to guide policy optimization in RL algorithms.
200	
201	    Args:
202	        data (DataProto): The data containing batched model outputs and inputs.
203	        adv_estimator (AdvantageEstimator): The advantage estimator to use (e.g., GAE, GRPO, REINFORCE++).
204	        gamma (float, optional): Discount factor for future rewards. Defaults to 1.0.
205	        lam (float, optional): Lambda parameter for GAE. Defaults to 1.0.
206	        num_repeat (int, optional): Number of times to repeat the computation. Defaults to 1.
207	        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo (bool, optional): Whether to normalize advantages by standard deviation in
208	            GRPO. Defaults to True.
209	        config (dict, optional): Configuration dictionary for algorithm settings. Defaults to None.
210	
211	    Returns:
212	        DataProto: The updated data with computed advantages and returns.
213	    """
214	    # Back-compatible with trainers that do not compute response mask in fit
215	    if "response_mask" not in data.batch.keys():
216	        data.batch["response_mask"] = compute_response_mask(data)
217	    # prepare response group
218	    if adv_estimator == AdvantageEstimator.GAE:
219	        # Compute advantages and returns using Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE)
220	        advantages, returns = core_algos.compute_gae_advantage_return(
221	            token_level_rewards=data.batch["token_level_rewards"],
222	            values=data.batch["values"],
223	            response_mask=data.batch["response_mask"],
224	            gamma=gamma,
225	            lam=lam,
226	        )
227	        data.batch["advantages"] = advantages
228	        data.batch["returns"] = returns
229	        if config.get("use_pf_ppo", False):
230	            data = core_algos.compute_pf_ppo_reweight_data(
231	                data,
232	                config.pf_ppo.get("reweight_method"),
233	                config.pf_ppo.get("weight_pow"),
234	            )
235	    elif adv_estimator == AdvantageEstimator.GRPO:
236	        # Initialize the mask for GRPO calculation
237	        grpo_calculation_mask = data.batch["response_mask"]
238	
239	        # Call compute_grpo_outcome_advantage with parameters matching its definition
240	        advantages, returns = core_algos.compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
241	            token_level_rewards=data.batch["token_level_rewards"],
242	            response_mask=grpo_calculation_mask,
243	            index=data.non_tensor_batch["uid"],
244	            norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo,
245	        )
246	        data.batch["advantages"] = advantages
247	        data.batch["returns"] = returns
248	    else:
249	        # handle all other adv estimator type other than GAE and GRPO
250	        adv_estimator_fn = core_algos.get_adv_estimator_fn(adv_estimator)
251	        adv_kwargs = {
252	            "token_level_rewards": data.batch["token_level_rewards"],
253	            "response_mask": data.batch["response_mask"],
254	            "config": config,
255	        }
256	        if "uid" in data.non_tensor_batch:  # optional
257	            adv_kwargs["index"] = data.non_tensor_batch["uid"]
258	        if "reward_baselines" in data.batch:  # optional
259	            adv_kwargs["reward_baselines"] = data.batch["reward_baselines"]
260	        # GDPO: pass raw data for per-dimension reward extraction
261	        if adv_estimator in (AdvantageEstimator.GDPO, "gdpo"):
262	            adv_kwargs["non_tensor_batch"] = data.non_tensor_batch
263	            adv_kwargs["batch"] = data.batch
264	        # Add sum_pi_squared for Optimal Token Baseline
265	        if adv_estimator in (AdvantageEstimator.OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE, AdvantageEstimator.TIR_OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE):
266	            # Check if sum_pi_squared is available
267	            assert "sum_pi_squared" in data.batch, (
268	                "Step-dependent optimal baseline requires sum_pi_squared from actor. "
269	                "Please set actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True in config."
270	            )
271	            adv_kwargs["sum_pi_squared"] = data.batch["sum_pi_squared"]
272	            # old_log_probs needed for path-variance proxy: w_t = 1 - 2*exp(old_log_probs) + sum_pi_squared
273	            adv_kwargs["old_log_probs"] = data.batch["old_log_probs"]
274	            # Get pre-computed rollout IS weights if available
275	            rollout_is_weights = data.batch.get("rollout_is_weights", None)
276	            adv_kwargs["rollout_is_weights"] = rollout_is_weights
277	
278	        # calculate advantage estimator
279	        advantages, returns = adv_estimator_fn(**adv_kwargs)
280	        data.batch["advantages"] = advantages
281	        data.batch["returns"] = returns
282	    return data

633	        - Non-tensor values are compared with standard equality

75	def repeat_kv(hidden_states: torch.Tensor, n_rep: int) -> torch.Tensor:
76	    """
77	    This is the equivalent of torch.repeat_interleave(x, dim=2, repeats=n_rep). The hidden states go from (batch,
78	    seqlen, num_key_value_heads, head_dim) to (batch, seqlen, num_attention_heads, head_dim)
79	    """
80	    batch, slen, num_key_value_heads, head_dim = hidden_states.shape
81	    if n_rep == 1:
82	        return hidden_states
83	    hidden_states = hidden_states[:, :, :, None, :].expand(batch, slen, num_key_value_heads, n_rep, head_dim)
84	    return hidden_states.reshape(batch, slen, num_key_value_heads * n_rep, head_dim)

87	def _ulysses_flash_attention_forward(
88	    query_states: torch.Tensor,
89	    key_states: torch.Tensor,
90	    value_states: torch.Tensor,
91	    attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor],
92	    query_length: int,
93	    *args,
94	    position_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
95	    **kwargs,
96	):
97	    """Insert all-to-all before and after flash attention.
98	    DeepSpeed-Ulysses: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.14509
99	
100	    For transformers>=4.55, the flash attention api has changed,
101	    we need to pass the query_length after doing ulysses all2all.
102	    See https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/40399
103	
104	    Args:
105	        query_states (torch.Tensor): (batch_size, seqlen/sp_size, nheads, head_dim)
106	        key_states (torch.Tensor): (batch_size, seqlen/sp_size, nheads_k, head_dim)
107	        value_states (torch.Tensor): (batch_size, seqlen/sp_size, nheads_k, head_dim)
108	        position_ids (torch.Tensor, optional): (batch_size, seqlen/sp_size)
109	
110	    Returns:
111	        torch.Tensor: (batch_size, seqlen/sp_size, nheads, head_dim)
112	
113	    """
114	    ulysses_sp_size = get_ulysses_sequence_parallel_world_size()
115	
116	    ########## AlltoAll for Ulysses ##########
117	    # TODO: Disable sp for ViT, there's no elegent way to determine whether it's ViT or not.
118	    # Use `position_ids` as condition since ViT doesn't pass it to flash attention.
119	    if ulysses_sp_size > 1 and position_ids is not None:
120	        # NOTE: repeat kv heads to be divided by sequence parallel. Instead of repeating nheads_q//nheads_k,
121	        # we choose to repeat sp_size//nheads_k, since flash_attention supports MQA/GQA.
122	        # For example:
123	        # - nheads_k=4, sp=8, repeats=2
124	        # - nheads_k=8, sp=8, repeats=1
125	        # - nheads_k=16, sp=8, repeats=1
126	        repeats = max(ulysses_sp_size // key_states.size(2), 1)
127	        key_states = repeat_kv(key_states, repeats)
128	        value_states = repeat_kv(value_states, repeats)
129	
130	        # (bsz, seq_len/n, n_head, head_dim) -> (bsz, seq_len, n_head/n, head_dim)
131	        query_states = gather_seq_scatter_heads(query_states, seq_dim=1, head_dim=2)
132	        key_states = gather_seq_scatter_heads(key_states, seq_dim=1, head_dim=2)
133	        value_states = gather_seq_scatter_heads(value_states, seq_dim=1, head_dim=2)
134	
135	        # TODO: all_gather position_ids because `prepare_fa2_from_position_ids` needs it, we can eliminate
136	        # this all_gather by passing cu_seq_lens_q, cu_seq_lens_k, max_length_k, max_length_q explicitly.
137	        # https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/33932
138	
139	        # (bsz, seq_len/n) -> (bsz, seq_len)
140	        position_ids_list = [torch.empty_like(position_ids) for _ in range(ulysses_sp_size)]
141	        torch.distributed.all_gather(position_ids_list, position_ids, group=get_ulysses_sequence_parallel_group())
142	        position_ids = torch.concat(position_ids_list, dim=-1)
143	
144	    # (bsz, seq_len, n_head/n, head_dim)
145	    query_length = query_states.size(1)
146	    attn_output = _flash_attention_forward(
147	        query_states, key_states, value_states, attention_mask, query_length, *args, position_ids=position_ids, **kwargs
148	    )
149	
150	    ########## AlltoAll for Ulysses ##########
151	    if ulysses_sp_size > 1 and position_ids is not None:
152	        # (bsz, seq_len, n_head/n, head_dim) -> (bsz, seq_len/n, n_head, head_dim)
153	        attn_output = gather_heads_scatter_seq(attn_output, seq_dim=1, head_dim=2)
154	
155	    return attn_output
